claude.rationale: This was a simplification/consolidation of two already-affiliated public entities: ENLC already indirectly controlled ENLK through common GP (EGP) and managing member (EMM), so controlling intent continued rather than being replaced. ENLK's operations were already conducted by ENLK's Operating Partnership subsidiaries under EGP/EMM's pre-existing management, so the customer-facing assets (T4) and their operating processes (T5) were never separated at closing — no product-vs-process mismatch (gap_45=0). Likewise the people/organization ran the same operations via the shared pre-existing officer corps, with management continuity built around EGP/EMM's officers and no need for a transition-services bridge, so process and organization stayed aligned (gap_56=0). The filing explicitly notes no new transition-services or shared-services agreement was created because operations already shared a substrate.
